scenarios.name: New sleep goal asks what and why
scenarios.message: I want to fix my sleep.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Ask one natural question that starts clarifying what they want to change and why it matters. Do not jump to a full experiment or metrics yet.
anti_patterns: asking for input and output metrics in the first reply

scenarios.name: External should gets personal why probe
scenarios.message: I should exercise because I know I should be healthier.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Gently probe for a more personal reason using one question. Do not moralize or accept obligation as the full why.

scenarios.name: Vague output metric gets concrete framing

state.whyItMatters: feel less wrecked in the morning

history.content: How will you know this is working? What would you actually see or measure?

scenarios.message: I guess I'll just know if I feel better.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Do not accept 'feel better' as enough. Offer one concrete measurable framing and ask if it fits or if they would describe it differently.
anti_patterns: accepting 'feel better' as the output metric
asking for a metric in technical language
moving to system design before metric clarity

scenarios.name: Confirmed observable metric moves to system design
scenarios.message: Yeah, phone-free bedtime nights is the right thing to track.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Acknowledge the confirmed output metric and move toward system_design by asking about prior attempts or what has broken before.
anti_patterns: asking for the same metric again
designing the daily action without prior-attempt context

scenarios.name: Previous attempt is reflected in system terms

state.goalStatement: keep showing up for the gym

history.content: Have you tried to work on this before? What happened?

scenarios.message: I go hard for a week, then miss one day and it all falls apart.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Reflect the breaking point in system terms and ask one question about the smallest daily action that could survive a hard day.

scenarios.name: Ambitious daily action gets smallest-version prompt

state.previousAttempts: tried long morning writing blocks and quit

history.content: What's the one thing you could do each day that would make this more likely to happen?

scenarios.message: I could write for two hours every morning.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Reflect that this is the strong version and ask for the smallest version they could do even on a hard day.
anti_patterns: accepting two hours as the daily action

scenarios.name: Stuck user gets two or three small input options

history.content: What's the one thing you could do each day that would make this more likely to happen?

scenarios.message: I don't know. I blank on this stuff.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Offer two or three small behavior options based on the known context and ask which fits. Keep them controllable input actions.
anti_patterns: leaving the user with an abstract open question
suggesting outcome metrics instead of actions
making the user design everything alone

scenarios.name: Confirmed daily action gets summary and ready/refine choice

state.goalStatement: stop revenge bedtime scrolling so mornings feel less foggy
state.inputMetric: put phone on desk before brushing teeth

scenarios.message: Putting the phone on my desk before brushing teeth feels doable.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Summarize Goal, Output metric, and Daily action in the specified format, present 2-week no-blame framing, and ask the ready-or-refine choice question.
anti_patterns: missing one of the three summary bullets

scenarios.name: Optimization phase simplifies concerns

state.outputMetric: days I know my account balance

scenarios.message: I worry I'll avoid it if the number looks bad.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Treat the concern as design iteration, simplify or strengthen the system, and ask one question about the refined version.

scenarios.name: Completed phase asks final start-date confirmation

state.goalStatement: keep showing up for the gym after motivation drops
state.inputMetric: put on gym clothes after work and go for 10 minutes

scenarios.expected_behavior: Show final preview with Goal, Output metric, Daily action, and Start date slot; include no-blame 2-week framing; ask whether to start today or another day.

scenarios.name: Given start date completes skill

state.inputMetric: put phone on desk before brushing teeth

history.content: Does this feel right? Want to start today, or is there a better day to begin?

scenarios.expected_behavior: Record tomorrow as experimentStartDate, acknowledge warmly in one sentence, and complete with collected state. Do not add extra advice.

scenarios.name: Day planning request hands off
scenarios.message: Actually I just need help planning today.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Recognize day planning is outside scope and hand off rather than starting a goal experiment.
anti_patterns: asking what life goal they want to change
planning the day inside this skill

scenarios.name: Existing experiment check-in does not restart skill
scenarios.message: I already have a sleep experiment going. I just want to check in on it.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Do not restart setup. Hand off or surface existing experiment context instead of designing a new one.
anti_patterns: ignoring that the experiment already exists

scenarios.name: Explicit cancellation ends the skill
scenarios.message: Stop. I don't want to set up an experiment right now.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Respect the stop request and cancel without another setup question.
anti_patterns: asking why they want to stop
